key_insight: For MPS-based quantum trajectory simulations, the cheapest unraveling is not the one with the lowest entanglement per trajectory, but the one that minimizes the combined cost of trajectory complexity and sampling effort.
engineering_relevance: This gives quantum simulation engineers a hardware-aware way to choose stochastic unravelings based on memory, runtime, and available parallelism rather than trajectory entanglement alone.
method: Decompose total simulation cost into memory per trajectory, runtime per trajectory, and sampling effort.
Define two inflation factors: bond-dimension inflation α and sampling inflation κ.
Estimate (α, κ) from small pilot runs to build decision maps for selecting the preferred unraveling.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports benchmarks across multiple noise channels and shows that the preferred unraveling changes with noise strength, time-step resolution, system size, and parallelism.
watch_item: The pilot-based (α, κ) estimates may not transfer cleanly if the system, noise model, or hardware constraints differ substantially from the benchmarked regime.
paper_title: Computational regimes in matrix-product-state-based quantum trajectory simulations
